passages.original: LXVI. Agareni, qui et Sarraceni, sicut Orosii [Boh. Eorosii) liber testatur, gens circumcisa a latere montis Caucasi, super mare Caspium, triram, Ircoliae a cognomento , jam olim consedentes, cum in nimia multitudine crevissent, tandem arma sumentes, provincias Heraclii imperatoris ad vastandam irruunl : contra quos Heraclius milites 640 ad resistendum direxil.
passages.english: 66. The Hagarenes, who are also [called] Saracens, as the book of Orosius testifies, a circumcised people from the side of Mount Caucasus, above the Caspian Sea, having long since settled in the land called Ercolia, when they had grown into an excessive multitude, at last took up arms and burst into the provinces of the emperor Heraclius to lay [them] waste; against them Heraclius sent soldiers to resist.
passages.notes: The words "triram, Ircoliae a cognomento" are corrupt; probably for "terram Ercoliae cognomento" ("the land called Ercolia/Hyrcania"), translated so. "[Boh. Eorosii)" is an editorial variant note and is omitted. "640" is a marginal date in the edition and is omitted. "irruunl" and "direxil" read as "irruunt" and "direxit".
